newsitem.title: USA: AT&T's Allen says he sees its stock as cheap.
newsitem.headline: AT&T's Allen says he sees its stock as cheap.

text.p: AT&T Corp Chairman Robert Allen said Wednesday that while the company's stock price has been diluted by the substantial investments the company is making in new markets, the stock remains undervalued and should be expected to head higher.
Speaking to reporters before the company's annual shareholders meeting here, Allen said, "I think the stock is cheap."
"I happen to believe that we are at a trough in our stock price and we are going the other way," Allen said in response to a reporter's question.

AT&T's stock, which closed at 34-1/4 Tuesday, near its year-low, has traded listlessly since the company unveiled a strategy to sharply increase investments in wireless and local service markets at a meeting in early March.

The company has warned these investments will depress earnings in the current and upcoming years and many Wall Street analysts believe the stock will remain "dead money" -- as one analyst has put it -- for the next year or two.

In comments to reporters, the top executive of the nation's leading long-distance company blamed the company's problems in part on confusion over the direction of the telecommunications industry in general.

But he also acknowlegded that the company had made mistakes in recent years in terms of executing its stated strategies and by moving dangerously close to competing with rivals on pricing instead of the quality of services.
Addressing himself to the company's shareholders, Allen said that "AT&T's stock price is their one concern and ours too."

Despite the stock's malaise, AT&T, or "Telephone" as it has long been known by stock traders, remains the nation's most widely held stock, with more than 3.3 million shareholders, according to a company spokesman.
